8.definition: Of or relating to Babylon and Babylonia — the central-southern Mesopotamian state, language, and culture centered on the city of Babylon. As an adjective it covers the Babylonians' Akkadian dialect, their gods and rituals, and the throne the Kassite kings inherited from Hammurabi's dynasty.

9.definition: Of or relating to Babylon and Babylonia — the central-southern Mesopotamian state, language, and culture centered on the city of Babylon. Here it covers the Babylonian priests and scribes who composed the Enuma Elish and mapped the sky after the Bronze Age Collapse.

10.definition: The grand royal palace King Ashurnasirpal II built at Nimrud in the 9th century BCE, its rooms lined with carved limestone relief panels showing military campaigns, royal hunts, and winged protective spirits.

Ashurnasirpal II's from-scratch building of a new Neo-Assyrian capital at Nimrud (Kalhu) on the middle Tigris — one of the largest construction projects in the ancient world up to that point, raised largely with deported labor and inaugurated by a famous ten-day feast for nearly 70,000 guests.

12.definition: A broad family of related peoples and languages of the Iranian plateau and Central Asia, including the Medes and Persians who would soon conquer Babylon. "Iranian" here is an ethnolinguistic label, not a reference to the modern nation-state.
